rows.comment: Opens with an unprompted reassurance and uses an em dash and the cute 'ping' phrasing. The useful fact is that the first notification adds the app and does not buzz.
lineComments: Replace the em dash and 'ping' with the mechanism: first notification adds the app silently, later ones can buzz.
rows.replacement: An app is added to this list the first time it notifies you while the relay is on. That first notification does not buzz the band. Later ones can.

rows.comment: Aphorism built on a 'not X' contrast nobody raised. A plain title names the topic.
lineComments: Rewrite as a plain heading for the buzz limits.

rows.comment: One long sentence stacking three rules with 'never' and 'at all'. Split into one rule per sentence; the four-second figure is kept.
lineComments: Split into three short rules and keep the four-second window.
rows.replacement: Repeat posts from the same app within four seconds are ignored. Ongoing notifications, such as media players and downloads, never buzz. Nothing buzzes while the band is disconnected.

rows.comment: Em dash and vague 'everything you typed in'. Say what the files contain and what each day records.
lineComments: Replace the dash with 'covering', name the typed-in data as manual entries, and split the last clause into its own sentence.
rows.replacement: {count} CSV files covering daily metrics, workouts, sleep, journal and labs, plus everything you entered by hand. Each day lists its data source and the algorithm version that scored it.

rows.comment: Fragments, an em dash, and 'lossless' without saying what it holds. The warning that anyone with the file can read it must stay.
lineComments: Keep the restore and readability facts and the exposure warning; drop the dash and fragments.
rows.replacement: One .db file with all your stored data. It is the only format that restores onto another phone. Anything that opens SQLite can read it, including anyone who gets the file.

rows.comment: Em dash and a 'because there is no account' aside. The no-recovery warning is needed and is kept; state it directly.
lineComments: Keep the no-recovery warning and the no-account fact as separate plain sentences.
rows.replacement: A complete copy encrypted with a passphrase, suitable for storing in iCloud. If you forget the passphrase, the file cannot be opened. There is no recovery, because there is no account holding a key.

rows.comment: States format, location and retention directly, including that the copy is unencrypted.
Lists accepted formats and states the overwrite rule, which the reader needs.
lineComments: Specific list of formats and a concrete data-safety rule.

rows.comment: 'Needed after' is vague passive-style phrasing. Tell the reader when to run it.
lineComments: Turn it into an instruction: when to run it.
rows.replacement: Scores every day again from stored data. Run it after a long-haul flight or after an import that added days out of order.

rows.comment: Short error title; the detail follows in the message.
States count and which sets failed.
Short confirmation that tells the reader the file holds everything.
Em dash and 'including us' flourish. The no-access warning stays.
lineComments: Keep that no one can open it without the passphrase; drop the dash and the 'us' aside.
rows.replacement: Encrypted backup shared. Without the passphrase nobody can open it, including this app.

rows.comment: 'Threw' is developer jargon and the sentence is long. Say the rows are saved, the rebuild failed, and what the user sees as a result.
lineComments: Split into saved rows and failed rebuild; replace 'threw' with 'failed'.
rows.replacement: All imported rows are saved. Rebuilding the cross-day summaries failed ({error}), so trends and insights still reflect your data from before the import.

rows.comment: Names the device types you can add.
Short setting title; the subtitle explains it.
'Abstain' is internal jargon for showing no value. Say the metrics stay blank.
rows.replacement: The phone counts steps and nothing else. Heart rate, sleep, recovery and temperature stay blank until a band is paired.

rows.comment: 'Abstain rather than estimate' is jargon plus an unraised contrast. State what the reader will see.
lineComments: Say metrics stay blank; drop 'rather than estimate'.
rows.replacement: No band is paired and no phone steps are arriving, so every metric in the app stays blank.

rows.comment: 'Ladder' is a metaphor; the items beneath are labeled 'Tier'. Name it the same way.
lineComments: Use the word the rows use: tiers.

rows.comment: Error with two concrete recovery conditions.
'Banked' is a cute metaphor, there is an em dash, and the closing 'removes the source, not the data' is a stacked antithesis. The data-kept statement must remain.
lineComments: State the consequence and that saved data stays; drop the dash, 'banked' and the antithesis.
rows.replacement: It is no longer used during workouts, and you must pair it again to use it. Data already saved on this phone is kept.

rows.comment: Same 'banked' metaphor, em dash and 'source, not the data' antithesis as the sensor dialog. The data-kept statement must remain.
lineComments: State consequence and that saved data stays; drop the dash, 'banked' and the antithesis.
rows.replacement: The band stops syncing, and you must pair it again to measure anything. Data already saved on this phone is kept.

rows.comment: Em dash and clipped fragment. Say plainly that it has not been tested on hardware and why.
lineComments: Keep the untested-hardware warning; replace the dash and 'nobody here' with a full explanation.
rows.replacement: Decoded from the protocol. It has not been tested on real hardware, because no one on the project owns one.

rows.comment: States what is stored and what is not used yet.
States what is stored and when, and that nothing is calculated from it yet.
